utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Are we ready, Mr. Borovic -- oh, Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we're ready. I'd like to call witness Paunovic. Could he please be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Would you please read aloud the affirmation that is on the card given to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon to all participants in the proceedings. Good afternoon to all in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Paunovic.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, please, before we start with this examination, please take into account some of the instructions I will give you. In order to have your testimony interpreted properly and recorded properly in the transcript, please wait for my question to end and then, after a while, could you please answer, so that you and I would not overlap, so that the questions and answers will not overlap. That way we'll just create confusion, and we really don't want to have any problems in the transcript. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Mr. Paunovic, to begin with, could you please tell the Honourable Trial Chamber and us your full name and surname, your date and place of birth, and your marital status, and your family situation.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 30th of January, 1956, in Ursule, municipality of Sjenica, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, could you please give us your full name and surname. We haven't heard that.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Radoje Paunovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, is it correct that you completed the military academy of the ground forces in 1979?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the period from 1979 until 1988 you served in the garrison in Zajecar?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in 1988 you were reassigned to the Guards Brigade, to the 1st Battalion of the military police?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in 1990 you were appointed deputy commander of the 2nd Battalion of the military police in the Guards Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: We will agree that the duty of the 2nd -- the commander of the 2nd Battalion of the military police is a duty that you assumed in 1991, and that, as for that duty, commander of the 2nd Battalion of the military police within the Guards Motorised Brigade, is a duty you held during the events in Vukovar in 1991.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Upon your return from Vukovar, that is to say the end of 1991, were you assigned to the command of the Guards Brigade in the teaching department?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In 1992, I was assigned to the teaching department of the Guards Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In 1994, were you in the corps of special units as desk officer for the units of the military police?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: According to the information that I have, in 1999 you were assigned to the command of the 72nd Special Brigade as desk officer for the units of the military police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In 2002, you were sent to the centre for training cadres for the military security service as commander of military police courses.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that as for the rank of major, you got it in 1993?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You were retired on the 22nd of July, 2005, as a colonel, and you got the rank of colonel in 2001; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, can we agree on the basis of all of this that in your military career you held responsible duties and posts from company commander, deputy battalion commander, battalion commander, and these duties that I mentioned, these posts that you held after your return to Vukovar, and these are military positions of responsibility. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: It can be put that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, let us now move on to the subject of this trial here and what we are all primarily interested in, and that is the events in Vukovar. We heard that you were commander of the 2nd Battalion of the military police within the Guards Motorised Brigade, when you were sent to Vukovar. What I'm interested in is the following, and what everybody here is interested in, could you please tell us and the Trial Chamber: When was it that you were sent to Vukovar with your battalion?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I was sent to Vukovar on the 30th of September, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you were sent to Vukovar, was your entire battalion sent there, the 2nd Battalion of the military police, or rather, was that battalion at its full complement when you were sent to Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: On the 30th of September, the entire battalion was sent to Vukovar but not under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what that means, the whole battalion but not under your command. Were some parts of the battalion somewhere else? Were they attached, resubordinated, to somebody else?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can explain that. This is how it happened: There were two companies, specifically the 1st and the 2nd one, under my command, and one company, specifically the 4th Company, according to the decision made by the brigade commander, was resubordinated to the armoured battalion of the Guards Brigade. The 3rd Company was engaged, according to platoons, in the following way: The 1st Platoon of the 3rd Company was resubordinated to the 1st Motorised Battalion of the Guards Brigade; the 2nd Platoon of the 3rd Company was resubordinated to the 2nd Motorised Battalion of the Guards Brigade; the 3rd Platoon of the 3rd Company was securing the rear command post of the Guards Brigade. That is my answer to your question as to how the battalion was engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me about the 4th Company.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I think I told you that the 4th Company was resubordinated to the armoured battalion of the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me who the commander of the 1st Motorised Battalion was? And one company from your battalion was resubordinated to that commander.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 1st Motorised Battalion was Major Tesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And who was commander of the 2nd Motorised Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 2nd Motorised Battalion was Major Adem Bajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was he commander all the time?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: During the initial period, as we were leaving from our peacetime location, it was Bajic, Major Bajic. But at the beginning of the month of October - I cannot remember the exact date now, of course - this duty was assumed by Lieutenant-Colonel Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, you mentioned your 3rd Company from the 2nd Battalion of the military police that was divided into platoons. I just did not hear about the 3rd Platoon. What was the duty of the 3rd Platoon of the 3rd Company? Where was it deployed? Perhaps you've said it. I am sorry. Oh, yes, they were providing security for the rear command post. Yes, thank you. Sorry about that. Your 2nd Battalion of the military police, was it taken into combat action?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In the initial period, that is to say, for some four or five days, the 2nd Battalion of the military police was a reserve of the brigade, and it was in the village of Berak, which is to say the 1st and 2nd Company, with a command and the signals squad and the logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Were you taken into combat action; if so, how?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: After four or five days, perhaps even less - now with this time distance, I cannot remember - I was given an order by the brigade commander to be ready with my battalion to go into combat, which is, indeed, what happened after these four or five days, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, were you taken into combat action as an independent establishment unit, the 2nd Battalion of the military police, or were you within some other composition; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: When I said that I was taken into combat action, in that period of time, I don't know up until when, I carried out my duties as a battalion. In the later period - again, I cannot give the exact dates - the 2nd Battalion of the military police became part of the 2nd Assault Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, would you tell me who the commander of the 2nd Assault Detachment was?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 2nd Assault Detachment was Lieutenant-Colonel Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you were brought into combat, as commander of the 2nd Battalion of the military police, did you have a command post of your own in Vukovar? If so, can you explain where this command post of yours was.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: When I was taken into combat action, of course I had a command post. It was in Prvomajska Street. I cannot remember the number now. Tentatively it's to the north, or perhaps a bit to the north-west of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, I'm just going to ask you another thing. You've already referred to it. You actually mentioned the 2nd Battalion, and as far as I understood you, the 2nd Battalion of the military police, where you were commander, had four companies. Did it have any other units within its composition?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the establishment of the battalion, in addition to these four companies, included the command of the battalion, the signals squad, and a logistics platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Paunovic. Now that we're on this subject, since some names may come up during your evidence, so in order for us to know what this is all about, could you tell us who the commanders, komandiri, of these four companies were, the 1st, 2nd, the 3rd, and 4th?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Milan Pavlovic was commander of the 1st Company. The commander of the 2nd Company was Captain Dragoslav Kapor. I'm sorry, I beg your pardon. The commander of the 2nd Company was Nenad Bajic. The commander of the 3rd Company was Captain Dragoslav Kapor. And the commander of the 4th Company was Captain Esad Paldum.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, you are convinced -- you were brought into combat in the manner that you described. Could you tell me, please -- it's been said that there's something wrong with the interpretation. You, Mr. Paunovic, described the way that you were brought into combat. You mentioned that you were part of the Assault Detachment 2, or 2nd Assault Detachment. Throughout your combat engagement, was this situation the same, that you were part of the 2nd Assault Detachment, or were you, at times, an independent entity of the 2nd Battalion in combat?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In the initial period, I was an independent battalion but within the brigade. In the subsequent period, over a longer period of time, I was part of the 2nd Assault Detachment. As far as I can remember, around mid-November, I acted independently; I wasn't part of the 2nd Assault Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Paunovic. I will not insist on an accurate time-line because I know that much time has lapsed and it's very difficult for you to remember. But if you can remember approximately some dates, please indicate so. Tell me, Mr. Paunovic, in accordance with the rules of service of the military police of the JNA, is it customary for military police to be used in combat? And before that question, whether the military police troops have the proper training for combat? And what is the predominant purpose of their training?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The military police is primarily trained for military police tasks. And during training, military policemen are trained to perform such tasks but not to such an extent as is the training of the performance of military police tasks. Military police primarily performs military police tasks pursuant to the rules of service of the military police of the armed forces, the rules of service and the guidelines for the applications of rules of service of the military police. But pursuant to a brigade commander's decision and order, military police may be used to perform other tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, as battalion commander, the commander of the 2nd Battalion of the military police, did you attend the reports being -- the briefings in the motorised brigades in Vukovar? And I'm referring to the period of 30th September until your return, and, if I'm not mistaken, that took place on the 24th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I did attend briefings at the command of the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: At these meetings at the command of the South Operative Group of the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade, did you receive any tasks? And could you explain to those present how this briefing looked like and how the issuance of tasks did take place at the OG level.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in brief, a briefing would look like this: Commanders of the subordinated units, subordinate to the brigade commander, would report on the conditions in their units, on the tasks achieved, tasks handed down to them, on problems, requirements, et cetera. Afterwards, the floor would be given to members of the command. The commander would recognise anybody seeking to take the floor, if he would be touring the units, to relay their opinions, their remarks and impressions. And finally, the commander of the brigade would issue tasks for the forthcoming period for the subsequent day. That would briefly be a cross-section of such briefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you received -- when you receive a task during a briefing for the forthcoming periods, one day or the subsequent several days, what you, as battalion commander, do after that? Do you, at your command post, hold a briefing, in turn, to elaborate that task further, or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, having been issued a task, I then, with my subordinated officers, company commanders, the commander of the logistics platoon, would elaborate these tasks further and I would issue them with concrete tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Paunovic. Now we are approaching the dates that are of great interest for all of us here. My first question refers specifically, if you may remember, whether, on the 19th of November, 1991, did you have a task, any task, which would refer to your activities in the area of the water-tower in the direction towards Mitnica? If so, could you explain what kind of a task it was, and when did you start performing this task?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: On the 19th of November, I received from the brigade commander a task to frisk and to search the area from the water-tower towards Mitnica. The task, and the reason for me performing this task, was to make sure whether some individuals from paramilitary formations had stayed behind; to detect and find unexploded mines, other explosive devices. And another task was to evacuate the population from that part of the town for their security's sake.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, I believe that one date is beyond questioning. We've heard this date so many times before. The day is the 18th of November, which is, depending on the perspective of the speaker, is the day when Vukovar was liberated or occupied. Could you take this date as reference to your explanations? Do you know anything about the surrender of the Mitnica Battalion on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: What I described just now is connected in my mind with the 19th of November, because I know that on the day before, on the 18th of November, the Mitnica group had surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During performing this task on the 19th of November, did you, during its performance, receive any other task; and if so, from whom?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: During the performance of this task that I described just now, I received a task from the brigade commander. And I don't believe I remember; I think the Chief of Staff did relay this order. And the order was to take a company of military police and to come with it to the area of the Vukovar Hospital, to take over the task of securing the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you set out to perform this task? And which units did you reach the hospital with?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I ordered the 4th Company commander - at this particular point in time that we're referring to, it was commanded by Captain First Class Simic Milivoje - to advance with his company towards the hospital, and this is exactly what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, lest there should be any doubt, you just stated that the 4th Company was commanded by Esad Paldum and now you are mentioning Mr. Simic. Can you give us an explanation.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The answer is the following: Either in the first or in the second half of October - I really cannot pinpoint any dates after so much time has lapsed - Captain Esad Paldum, the then-commander of the 4th Company, fell ill. And from that point on until we returned to Belgrade, the 4th Company was commanded by Captain First Class Simic Milivoje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Paunovic. Let us make this clear, lest there should be any doubt about that. Can you tell me, if you remember, during that day, the 19th of November, when did you reach the Vukovar Hospital compound?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact hour, but it was in the afternoon. Afternoon, around 1400, 1500 hours. I know that it was still daylight; it hadn't grown dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "it hadn't grown dark," does it mean that relatively quickly after your arrival, dusk fell?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm just sorting out these facts in my mind. I know which activities we performed upon our arrival, how long it took us. So I believe this is the hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you tell us, when you arrived with this company, commanded by Captain Simic, on the 19th, did you come upon any present -- any JNA commander officer already present at this date; and if you could indicate the unit that they came from?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived in the area of the hospital, I found Major Sljivancanin, Major Tesic, and I believe a Captain Bojkovski was there as well. This is as far as I remember when it comes to the officers that I saw in the area of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you'd arrived to perform a task issued by the brigade commander, that you had arrived with a company of soldiers to secure the area of the hospital. Could you conclude that prior to your arrival there had been some security apparatus that you took over from, and could you assess the situation?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived to the area of the hospital, as I said, I already saw that person and I contacted him, and that was Major Tesic. He showed me where his soldiers were deployed. I cannot remember now how many soldiers there were. But talking about security, in military police terms, there was no security in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that "security, in military police terms," can you explain what that means, to provide security for a facility in military police terms?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: When I said that it had not been provided in military police terms, and Major Tesic also told me about this, elements of this security could not seen there, the security that we're talking about; namely, entrance posts, patrols, guards, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you issue any order to Captain Simic related to the security of the hospital; and if so, what was that order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: As for the commander of the 4th Company, Captain Simic, I issued him an order to search the area surrounding the hospital and to set up security.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you say search the area of the hospital, what does that mean? And why is that done?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: According to our rules, when security is set up for any facility, the area is searched, and it is only then that the security is set up. In this case, the search was carried out in order to perhaps find some paramilitary groups or formations that had been left behind; also, to find mines, booby-traps; and also for the security to function properly and safely.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, is there a rule in these instructions about the work of the military police, or, generally speaking, is there a document of this kind or is it really a matter that the commander assesses, what area will be searched, what is the diameter, 5, 10 metres, 50 metres, or whatever?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it depends. It depends on the facility that is being secured. It depends on the configuration of the terrain, the combat activities that had taken place in that area beforehand. In this specific case, the area was searched to the left and right of the said facility, namely the hospital, 2 to 300 metres, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, did you have any information before you came to the area of the hospital in terms of a possibility of having disguised members of Croatian paramilitary forces in the hospital? If you did have such information, how had you received it? Where did you hear about this?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: As for this information that you're referring to, we got it from the security organs; namely, that it is very likely that, in the hospital itself, in addition to patients, there are also disguised members of paramilitary formations, of the paramilitary formations of Croatia, that is. As for their exact number, at that point in time, I did not have any information.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was this information one of the reasons, too, for you to search the terrain in that diameter or in that perimeter?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: That was the primary reason. And also, what I said a few moments ago, namely that there was this possibility that even outside the hospital, there could be some left-over individuals or groups, members of the paramilitary formations of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, we have information, I think that there is no doubt about that, but I'm going to ask you the following: What was the situation like in the hospital? Who was in the hospital? Was it only the sick and the wounded who were in the hospital, or were there some other structures that you saw?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: There's no doubt that in the hospital, in addition to the sick and wounded and the hospital staff, there were also members of the paramilitary formations of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any civilians in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: There were civilians, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When searching the terrain, did you find anything that would indicate that in that area there were armed individuals, armed groups or formations?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: During the search of the area around the hospital, parts of military equipment were found. A certain amount of light weaponry was found. When I say that, I'm referring to pistols and rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps have some information about where weapons could be found due to the stay of these armed individuals, or rather, did you perhaps get this information from civilians, from local people? Because there was quite a bit of commotion there - that's my understanding - that there were lots of people there.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as you said, there was great commotion there. In addition to this information that I had received, as I already mentioned, there was also information received from civilians; namely, they were saying that weapons were thrown away. "Take a look at this." They did not tell us exactly where to look, but as we searched the area, as I've said, we did find a certain quantity of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You said that, Mr. Paunovic. I'm only interested in this: Whether you received any information from the local people. Did you have any information, and did you perhaps go to a particular area or particular place where somebody indicated to you that perhaps this could be a place where some command of some parliament formations had been --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: -- do you remember any such thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is outside the first preliminary notes provided by the Defence on November 1st. This is outside the second preliminary notes provided on November 2nd. This question is outside of the 65 ter information as to what this witness is going to testify to, on the 12th of July. And it's outside of the amended 65 ter information as to what this witness was going to testify to on the 4th of August, 2006. The first time this issue was ever even raised was last week in the testimony of Mr. Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I must admit that, if we look at it this way, the Prosecutor is right. But I think that we have a witness who gave an order to his company to search an area, and this has to do with what the Prosecutor referred to as well. If you think that I cannot proceed with this line of questioning, no problem whatsoever. I won't do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it's best left, Mr. Bulatovic, in view of the number of identifications of the areas of potential evidence and this one being outside of all of them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, do you know about this day, the 19th of November, when you were providing security, were any members of paramilitary formations surrendering or was anybody surrendering in the hospital area? Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I do not have any such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Will you tell me about what you found, these parts of equipment, weapons, arms, and so on? Did you inform the security organ about that, specifically Mr. Sljivancanin, whom you did see there within the hospital compound, once you arrived?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, of course I informed the security organ about that. In this case, it was Major Sljivancanin, because at that point in time he was physically close to where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is it your duty, is it your obligation, to inform the security organ about such matters?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is compulsory, and I did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say that you came to the area of the hospital on the 19th of November, around 1500 hours. Do you remember how long you stayed there and whether, in the meantime, up until the end of your stay, whether you went somewhere? If so, where did you go, how many times? To the best of your recollection, can you explain this to us. Can you tell us about your movements on the 19th, from the hospital onwards.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: From when I came to the hospital on the 19th of November all the way up to 2400 hours, I left the hospital a few times and came back to the hospital a few times. The first reason why I left was the fact that I was supposed to go - and, indeed, I did go - to the brigade command for a briefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, sorry for interrupting. When you say "a briefing," can you explain what this means? Was there a customary time when these briefings took place? And then please go on.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as I can remember, the briefings took place around 1800 hours, 1800 hours, yes. May I proceed, Mr. Bulatovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, about this briefing on the 19th, and how long you stayed there.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: When I went to the briefing, I stayed there for about two hours --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, sorry for interrupting. After that, what did you do; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: After that, I returned to the hospital. I called the company commander and gave him some tasks to continue securing the hospital. As for the commander of the 1st Company, I told him to prepare a platoon and send it to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This platoon that was to be sent to the hospital, was it to be sent on that day, the 19th of November, or perhaps some other day? I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was not precise enough. I gave the company commander a task, namely to prepare the platoon, but to send it to the hospital area in the early morning hours of the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you returned to the hospital after the briefing, two hours later, what would the time be when you returned to the hospital, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot specify an hour after such a long time has lapsed. I believe that it was possibly 2000, 2100 hours. I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: At that briefing on the 19th of November, 1991, in the command of the Guards Brigade, did you see Major Veselin Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you returned to the hospital, did you see Major Sljivancanin at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the briefing, Mr. Paunovic, that briefing on the 19th of November. I'm interested in certain matters. You explained the way a briefing would unfold, what is the procedure, what is the schedule. What I'm interested in is the following: Do you recall, on the 19th of November, in the evening, was there any talk at the OG staff and 1st Motorised Brigade level, if there was any talk about the evacuation of the Vukovar Hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: There was talk about that. It was said that on the 20th of November the hospital will be evacuated, but I don't remember any time being specified for that activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear at the command post of the JUG of south operational group the name of Major Sljivancanin to command the forthcoming evacuation of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I'd object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've coming very close to the major issues in the case and these should be non-leading questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, was there any talk at the briefing in the OG South command about the identity of the officer to command the evacuation of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No names were specified as to who would command the operation of evacuating the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us - and we heard from your CV you are a person who held positions of responsibility - could we hear from you, should there have been a written order for such a task, or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, there should have been a written order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: As a competent person who held positions of responsibilities and duties -- responsible duties, could you tell us, such a task, what would it entail? What services, what structures, would have to be engaged? And what elements of such an order should there be?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: As you said yourself, this is a very complex operation and such an operation should involve all segments of the brigade, and by this I mean the following: The brigade command, logistics; military police should be involved; security organs, and similar. And an order to this effect should comprise the following elements; of course I cannot remember all of them, but I will spell out the basic ones: So the commander should appoint a responsible officer who would be in charge of the evacuation. Other personnel from the command who would be involved in the area of logistics, what should be regulated are vehicles, means of transportation, food, medical care. As far as organs of security are concerned, they are supposed to triage the personnel, together with physicians, all the people present. Another thing that slipped my mind, if one has the list of people in the hospital, it should be specified whether such persons are armed, whether they present a threat, et cetera, et cetera. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: On the occasion of any type of evacuation, not this one, when people are transported, does the military police play a role in accompanying such people? And what is the purpose of such an escort?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: During such and similar operations, the task for the military police is to secure the persons being transported, which would mean the following, pursuant to our rules: The reception of these persons, maintaining security of them during transport, and delivering them to the competent organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, on the 19th, you were at the hospital, and from your testimony and from exhibits, we heard testimony about the conditions in the hospital. What I'm interested in is the following: Were there members of, let's call them so, paramilitary formations, Territorial Defence, armed civilians, around the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Around the hospital there were civilians dressed in various clothes. Some were armed with light weaponry. You know, at that time, almost everybody was carrying arms. They were in groups of four or five people. I really cannot specify the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What was their conduct? Could you describe their conduct.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say that their conduct was violent, but they did issue provocations. Individuals wanted -- I mean, asked whether they could enter the hospital. They shouted. There were curses as well. I really cannot remember every detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you said "curses," who were these curses directed at?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Everybody, including members of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Why? What did they utter to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The most frequently used expression used by that population was communist, or komunjara.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the reason why they used that term? What was the association in their minds for using that term?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what. Presumably because of the insignia that we wore, a five-pointed red star, JNA, Yugoslav People's Army insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, could you tell me, please, what was your opinion of these groups? You made your views public on these. What term did you use to denote them?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Since I communicated personally with some of them, I did not regard them as a threat, as dangerous, as people who may jeopardise the security and safety of the hospital and the hospital itself. In some of my previous statements, I referred to them as model Chetniks, or Chetnik models.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "Chetnik models," could you explain to the Court why you coined this phrase. Who were those people, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In my regard, in my opinion, these people were among the local population. They were not fighters. I believe that they didn't even engage in combat. And, in my opinion, they did not constitute any danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, I have a hypothetical question for you. If you concluded, as a person in charge of the security of the hospital that these people presented a threat, what would you, as an officer in charge, have done?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I would buff up the security around the hospital, and I would have reported immediately to the brigade commander. But in this case, I did not report to the brigade commander because, according to my estimate, as I already stated, they did not constitute a threat, neither to my security personnel, nor to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You recently said, Mr. Paunovic, that, on the 19th, you received a task to reinforce, with a platoon or a part of a company, the security detail around the hospital on the subsequent day. Do you know the reasons why you were issued with such an order? I don't want to lead you. You know the reason. Please tell us, if you know.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Previous -- in response to previous questions, I believe I replied to this. I said that on the 20th the evacuation of the hospital was supposed to start, and, given that I had one company securing the hospital but that company was not at its full complement and I knew that I would be needing personnel to provide escort to vehicles, carrying the evacuees. Furthermore, I needed men to frisk people upon leaving the hospital, and to avoid undermining the overall security system I ordered for this platoon to be involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree, Mr. Paunovic, that this reinforcement of security had nothing to do with the greater threat? We're dealing with military police operations.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Had there been any threats, I would have informed the brigade commander immediately and would have requested reinforcements; or, alternatively, I would have reinforced, using my men, to buff up the security and would have informed the brigade commander immediately. But in this case, I believe that I've already provided an answer to this, to wit: My assessment was that the civilians and persons located around the hospital did not pose a threat to the security apparatus and system.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would it be the right time for the first break, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bulatovic, yes. We will resume at ten past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, we were talking about the 19th, so we've basically dealt with that subject; however, there are a few other things that I'd like to ask you about the 19th. Do you remember some corpses around the hospital, having seen some corpses around the hospital, when you got there, around 1500 hours?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the corpses. There were some near the hospital; as a matter of fact, even outside the hospital compound. As for the number of corpses, I could not say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Since obviously we have this big time distance, and it's probably hard for you to remember the actual time and other things, but let's try, let's have an approximation. Was it 20, 30, 50, more, less? Can you give us an approximation?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: There certainly weren't less than 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that's when you came there, so it was daylight, right? Not at night. You cannot really conduct a search at night. Do you remember whether Mr. Sljivancanin saw these corpses together with you when touring the area around the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This is leading. And there was never any evidence about Sljivancanin touring the hospital, the area around the hospital either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is technically leading, Mr. Bulatovic, although I don't see it's as significant as Mr. Weiner fears. If you could try and watch the leading. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right, Your Honour. That was my feeling, too, that it wasn't really that dangerous and there was no reason for Mr. Weiner to be afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So now I'm going to ask the witness whether somebody went together with him to see those corpses.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the officers from my battalion, as I said in my previous answers, in the compound of the hospital, there was Major Sljivancanin, and he also saw those corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, during your stay there, that is to say when you went to that briefing, again, I mean, I'm not going to refer to any specific time because it really has been quite a while, and I know that during the proofing there was this problem of remembering the actual time, so I'm not going to ask you about time specifically. I will try to link things to certain events, certain things that happened. So when you went from the hospital to that briefing, did you see the representatives of the International Red Cross at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Before I went to the briefing, I saw representatives of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for this representative of the International Red Cross who you saw on the 19th, at that time, that is to say up until you went to the briefing, did you perhaps see this person the following day in the hospital too?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this same gentleman I had seen that evening. I don't know his name. I saw him on the next day, in the morning; that is to say, on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I said that I'm not going to refer to any specific time, so this is the only thing I was interested in. On that day, the 19th, when you saw the representatives of the Red Cross and hospital, did you see anyone talking to them? Specifically, was Mr. Sljivancanin talking to them?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The gentleman was speaking to Sljivancanin. He was in Sljivancanin's company, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: While you were at the hospital and up until the moment when you went to this briefing, did you receive any orders, any instructions, to take some person out of the hospital? Just say yes or no, please. Let us keep things as brief as possible. We have a problem with time and we want to be as efficient as possible.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you take the person from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the person?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The person's name is Marin Vidic, Bili.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you take him?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I took him to Negoslavci, and I handed him over to the desk officer of the security organ, an NCO. Momcilovic, specifically, Momcilovic, I know who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Paunovic, let us now move on to the 20th of November. Do you remember on the 20th you came there in the morning hours, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, the platoon or the reinforced platoon, whatever the formation was, had already arrived in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This platoon, this formation, did it have an officer of its own?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Lieutenant Milomir Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was he your subordinate?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: At that moment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: As for that officer and the soldiers from that platoon, reinforced platoon --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the speaker please not touch the microphone, Mr. Bulatovic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: -- did you issue him any orders to carry out some military police work?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I gave them a task to carry out some military police work, and that is to say frisk persons while they were being taken out of the hospital. That is to say, that this took place in front of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you perhaps describe this military police work of the frisking.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could Mr. Bulatovic please not touch the microphone while it's on.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: After the triage was carried out, groups were taken out of the hospital. Now, as for the size of the groups, I cannot say, but it was up to ten people. They would be lined up, up against a wall, because near that exit there is a wall opposite the hospital. And every one of these individuals was frisked by a soldier, a military policeman. Nearby there was a table where objects that were taken away from these individuals were put. When this would be completed, the group would be sent to the buses that were behind the hospital. Now, I cannot say --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, we'll get to the buses. I'm interested in this particular part now. Now, the frisking of these persons was carried out by members of the company or the platoon that is immediately subordinated to you. You are their first or second superior officer, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Specifically, in this particular case, I am the second superior officer to these soldiers. As for the company commander that we referred to, I am his immediate superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you issue an order to have these persons frisked, or was this order issued by somebody else?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand your question - would you care to clarify it - about this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Who issued the order to have these persons who were taken out of the hospital frisked?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't need any kind of order to do that, not to go back to what we have already said, what our assumptions were, who was in the hospital. As for the frisking, that is part of military police work. Specifically, that is one of the powers or duties of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a specific action, a complicated action, or is it an ordinary, routine thing?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: It is not a very complicated thing to do. We cannot say that it's just a routine thing, but we can say that it is normal military police work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how long the frisking of these individuals took? Again, I'm telling you, yet again, I am fully aware of the fact that it's been 15 years and that a great many things happened. But can you tell us approximately? It doesn't have to be the exact time.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, roughly, this lasted for about two hours; perhaps a bit more than that. But something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: A few moments ago you said that you didn't need any kind of order to do that kind of thing, but soldiers cannot just do it on their own. Do we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you issue an order to the soldiers to carry out this military police work?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Sljivancanin before that, in the morning, in the hospital, on the 20th?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Sljivancanin issuing an order to someone, to anyone?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that. If he was issuing an order to someone, it could have only been me, but I never received such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can a security organ issue any kind of order to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, it cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of November, did you see, as you saw -- that you had seen, the same representative of the International Red Cross that you saw on the 19th, in the morning of the 20th, together with Sljivancanin? Could you please be more specific as to the time when you saw him on the 20th in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact time that I saw that person. The only thing, I can try to tie it to some actions or activities. I saw him at the moment, approximately, towards the end of the frisking.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, could you recollect, where did you see him in the hospital? In the courtyard, close to the entrance? Can you specify the location within the hospital compound?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Within the hospital compound is where I saw him, very close to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him talk with anybody within the compound? Specifically, did you see him talk to Mr. Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I saw him, he was talking to Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How far were you at the time from them?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall, 5 to 10 metres. Relatively close but not that close.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was it an amicable or inamicable conversation that you -- they were having, in your opinion, as far as you could see on the basis of their gestures, tone, if you heard or did not hear the words themselves?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when I think back, I believe this was a normal conversation, nothing special. There were some other people, journalists, representatives of I don't know who, around them; they were not the only people. It was a normal conversation, although I don't know the content.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you say there were other representatives there, which representatives do you mean?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: They were representatives of the International Red Cross. Maybe observers. There were journalists. I don't know how to label these organisations. I don't know their titles from this time distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of November, did you see any other JNA officers in the hospital, irrespective of the time that you spent there on the 20th?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I did see -- well, there were many, maybe not many, but there were officers. I don't know their names. I remember one particularly, since I knew him personally. I still know that person. Nebojsa Pavkovic is his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, you mentioned some buses. Where were they parked or stopped? Could you specify, with reference to the hospital entrance, from where persons frisked by your unit were?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the name of the street. They were perpendicular to the hospital. And the persons frisked by our troops headed towards the buses, in a straight line.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is it known to you whether members of the military police from the unit subordinated to you provided security service around these buses?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On each coach there were two military policemen, pursuant to my order, to secure said coaches.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You issued an order to members of the military police from your unit to secure the buses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What does the specific order that you issued encompass? What was the task of the military policemen escorting those buses?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The soldiers and the policemen were given an order to secure the persons on those buses, primarily to make sure that such persons would not attack the driver or other members; second -- or one of the tasks was to prevent these persons from being attacked from without.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a real threat of an attack, or would it be a presumed threat, pursuant to the rules of service of the military police?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: At that point in time there was no danger of an attack, but as I already explained previously, pursuant to rules, escort activities in place the reception of escorted persons, securing during transport, and handing over of such escorted persons. And in the second element, or the second activity, rules of service envisage, if there is a presumption of an attack against these escorted persons, military policemen have the duty to protect them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, you issued an order to the soldiers of your unit to frisk such people; you ordered them to escort the buses. Did you notice, during issuing such orders, that there were any groups that may present -- pose a threat to the persons who were being led onto the buses?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not notice any persons who may pose a threat to the execution of this activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you issue an order to soldiers to escort buses, carrying escorted persons in whichever form, until which point this task is valid? At which point -- until which point is it in force?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In certain cases, and in this one, it cannot be specified in terms of duration, but it is in force, that order, until the escorted persons are handed over to the competent organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is it known to you whether officers are appointed to be on the vehicles carrying people who are being either escorted or evacuated?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Officers are appointed for each bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who appoints them?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The brigade commander in this case, I presume.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do soldiers escorting a bus, while on the bus, do they receive orders from that officer or somebody else? Is it known to you or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: When this task of escorting begins, soldiers do receive orders from that officer because they don't have anybody else to receive orders from. I, as battalion commander, company commander, am not in their presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Of course it is clear to us that there is a distance between you and them. You stayed behind at the hospital, et cetera. I had to clarify this. You said that you had received information that there were in the hospital disguised members of the paramilitary forces. Did you have any information, what was their disguise?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain this question to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will. They were disguised into somebody else. Do you know what their disguise was, the disguise of the members of paramilitary Croatian forces? What were they -- what was their guise? What kind of information you received?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I received information that they were disguised as patients, as injured people, as medical staff, and such-like.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is it known to you, Mr. Paunovic, that before frisking, performed by members of your unit, there had been a triage of such persons in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Before the frisking that you're referring to, within the hospital, triage was executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who did the triage of wounded or who could check whether somebody was really wounded or not? Who can verify that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Physicians, doctors performed that task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I did not ask you before: Do you know how many buses were there?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure I cannot specify a number. Maybe four, five, even more, but I did not see all of those buses in the vicinity of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you what uniforms people from your unit wore.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the military police, of the 2nd Battalion of the military police, wore olive-drab uniforms, so a single colour, not variegated. They had no special marks, in terms of the uniform they wore, from other members of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did they wear any special insignia or parts of their uniform that would distinguish them from other members of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to equipment, members of the military police, in performance of military police tasks and duties, wear the following items of equipment, such as: White belt, rubber baton, handcuffs, and such-like.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: May I ask you, Mr. Paunovic, you see the buses; you provide troops to escort the buses and secure the buses. Do you have information at that point where these buses are headed, with the persons being evacuated from the hospital after being frisked by your men?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I had information that the persons who had been frisked and sent to the buses would be transported to the Vukovar barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know why they were headed there? Could you tell us more about what you know about that.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, since, in the vicinity of the barracks, there is a facility, the Velepromet facility, in accordance with my information, persons who had to be taken from that facility had to be merged with the persons from said buses to be transported to Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know why it was Sremska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at that time the prisoner -- the prison, as well as the camp for prisoners of war, was in that town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, did your unit provide security for some civilians who were being transported from Mitnica? Did you work on their evacuation to Croatia and further on?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the 2nd Battalion were providing security in several directions, of civilians, that is. It had to do with the direction leading to Croatia. Who wanted to go to Croatia went to Croatia; then in the direction of Novi Sad and I don't know what other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there were some problems regarding the sending of these convoys to Croatia, that they were returned by Croats and that they had to go about things like that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember the date. There were such cases. So these convoys were returned. Now, where they went after that, did they go to Sid or back to Croatia, I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Paunovic. Of course, if you don't know something, then I'm not going to ask you about it. Let me ask you about the locality of Ovcara. Do you know where it is and do you know what it is?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I know where it is, this particular location, that is. Ovcara is a farm, a farm, an agricultural estate, depending on what people call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that every brigade, every unit, has its own area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know about the locality of Ovcara? On the 20th of November, 1991, do you know in whose area of responsibility it was, in the area of responsibility of what brigade, that is?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: At that point in time, it was in the area of responsibility of the 80th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who the commander of that brigade was?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the brigade was Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether this brigade had any military police establishment; and if so, what it was?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Specifically, the 80th Brigade had a company of military police within it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the difference is, Mr. Paunovic, between that brigade and the Guards Motorised Brigade, or between the Guards Motorised Brigade and some other brigade, a mountain brigade, an infantry brigade, an alpine brigade, and so on? Do you know what the difference is in terms of this establishment related to military police?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The difference between the Guards Brigade and some other brigade with regard to the military police is, first and foremost, reflected in establishment and then in the mode of commanding military police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain both, in the briefest possible terms.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The Guards Brigade has two battalions of military police. Some other brigade, like the ones you mentioned, has a company of military police. In the Guards Brigade, battalion commanders are commanded by the brigade commander, and in the military police company, in this other brigade, whatever it may be, the company is commanded by the security organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Under the authority of the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Now we are clear. Mr. Paunovic, I've asked you this quite a few times but I'm going to ask you yet again so that we will have completed that subject: Did you ever hear at any of the briefings attended by battalion commanders and other officers, motorised battalions, military police battalions, that anyone ever reported that Veselin Sljivancanin, as security organ, ever issued anyone any kind of order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never heard of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What about you? During your stay in Vukovar, in the contacts that you had, did Veselin Sljivancanin ever issue any order to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, he never issued any order to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, during your stay in Vukovar, did you have any contact with Veselin Sljivancanin in terms of him touring your command post and your unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had contacts when the unit was toured and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what the reasons were, why Veselin Sljivancanin came to your command post and to your unit. What was the point of these visits of his, if I can call them that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The point of his visit primarily had to do with security problems, if any. He always asked whether there were any problems. He asked about the situation in the battalion from the point of view of security. He would talk to the soldiers and officers that he was seeing. That would be it, in the briefest possible terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: While you and your unit were in Vukovar, in the 2nd Battalion of the military police, did you have any problems that required notification of the command and the commander of the unit; and if so, could you explain what it was.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: At one point in time, specifically, sometime around the 4th of November, I had some problems in the unit regarding morale and security. I can explain that. Since, at that time, the 45-day tour of duty of reserve soldiers was up in our units, they were supposed to go back to Belgrade. The assistant brigade commander for morale informed the other troops, that is to say, regular soldiers, that they would be sent to Belgrade too. Since they were not sent to Belgrade, of course, the soldiers protested. Some individuals left the positions. I informed the brigade commander about this, and, on the following day, he sent the Chief of Security, Major Sljivancanin, to the positions of my battalion. He had a meeting with the officers and soldiers. After that, the soldiers returned to the positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, you mentioned that your unit was providing security for the civilians on the 19th and the transport of civilians who were going to Croatia, and then we have the situation of the 20th, and so on. Do you know that some unit of yours provided security in the area of Velepromet; and if so, do you know in what period?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As for the Velepromet facility, external security was carried out by parts of my unit. As far as I can remember now, I think it was from the 20th onwards, up until the end of our stay in Vukovar, that is to say, up until the 24th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "the 20th," what month are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the month of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Who took over the security of the hospital after the 24th?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The security of the hospital, on the 24th of November, was taken over from the 2nd Battalion of the military police by the company of military police of the 80th Motorised Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when the 80th Brigade was brought into the area of Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was around the 18th of November, 1991, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, I didn't ask you something. Do you know whether Sljivancanin toured any other units? I am only talking about this period up until the 20th, that period up until the 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, he did tour other units. He didn't only tour my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How come you know that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I know that primarily from the briefings, because when I explained the technical aspect of briefings, in the briefest possible terms, I said that members of the brigade command presented their observations from their tours of different units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Were these security-related observations or some other observations?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, primarily security-related observations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, how many times did you give statements related to what happened in Vukovar, and to whom?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I gave my first statement in January 1999, at the military court in Belgrade. I gave my second statement in April 2005, in the special court in Belgrade. Then, in July 2005, I gave a statement at the office of the investigator from The Hague in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion you -- or, rather, were you then asked about all of these relevant matters pertaining to the events about which you're testifying here today?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Paunovic, you spoke in those statements, and today, about your contacts with Veselin Sljivancanin. I'm interested in your personal opinion of Veselin Sljivancanin as an officer.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I think I am not competent enough to assess him, but since you asked me, I believe, I think, that he was professional, good. Nothing bad to say about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I should have maybe asked you this at the very beginning: What was the reasons for the Guards Brigade to be sent to Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The reason for the Guards Brigade going to Vukovar was -- as far as I can say, followed from the commander of the brigade's order. One of the tasks was to lift the blockade of the JNA barracks in Vukovar and the liberation of the Vukovar population from paramilitary forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Whose?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The paramilitary forces of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, what was the ethnic composition of the Guards Motorised Brigade and your battalion, as part of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The ethnic composition of the Guards Brigade and of my battalion, the 2nd Battalion of military police, was multi-ethnic. To be more specific, I have information about the brigade, but I'm much more familiar with the situation in my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, with regard to Mr. Sljivancanin, your contacts with him, you said the multi-ethnic composition, you were speaking about terms that you were thrown at by the so-called Chetnik models who labeled you commies. Do you know what was Mr. Sljivancanin's position on these people?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can't really say which term he would use, but I'm sure that he neither liked them nor sympathised with them, because, in our opinion, a synonym for Chetnik is one pertaining to traitors, because we are dealing with the experiences from World War II.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Paunovic, I'm not going to elaborate on this topic. I was interested in Mr. Sljivancanin's opinion of that. Do you know if Mr. Sljivancanin had any contacts with the TO, pursuant to any line of command?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see, ever, Mr. Sljivancanin with any representative of the TO?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned in your testimony the presence of international representatives in the hospital; then some journalists, TV crews, et cetera. One of your statements given to the representatives of the Prosecution - I will not waste time on all of these, but may I remind you - you spoke about the media appearance of Mr. Sljivancanin and you had some criticism of that. Could you explain the situation to us, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Your question pertains to what statements I made. What I thought then I think now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And that is?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Which is reflected in the following: Sljivancanin was in love with the media, and media, being media, are prone, for reasons of increased circulation and whatnot, to exaggerate certain things, so that in the domestic public and among the international public as well, an impression was created that Sljivancanin was the top man; that there were no other people in charge, that he was the top dog. And on several occasions in the media, you could hear it said that he was the brigade commander, that he was commander of this, that, or the other thing, and such-like.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And, in reality, how far removed was Mr. Sljivancanin from the top man? A little or a lot?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
