utterances.text: He was one of the assistants to the commander. He was in charge of security.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So we can deduce that quite a lot of distance was between him and the top man.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, I'm going to ask you a couple of things with regard to the indictment. You had contacts with Sljivancanin; you had contacts with Mr. Mrksic, commander of the Guards Brigade; with other officers at the command post, whenever you received your tasks and on other occasions. Did you ever, during your stay in Vukovar, or at such briefings or meetings, or in any other way, attend anything? Or did you hear anything that may indicate an agreement for any action to be directed against the non-Serb population in terms of torture, extermination, murder, expulsion from territory? Did you ever attend such a meeting? Do you know anything about that? Or during your stay there, you could feel that somebody may be harbouring such plans in their mind?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never could conclude that such a thing would be at work. And from the brigade commander to the last soldier, we treated the population equally.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I've just concluded my examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bulatovic. Mr. Domazet, do you have questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do have some questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are they likely to take more than five minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will break now, then, and I'll allow you to commence after the break. We will resume, I hope, at a quarter to, but I'm once again having to see the President and I may be a little delayed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening, Mr. Paunovic. My name is Vladimir Domazet, one of the Defence counsel of Mr. Mrksic, and on behalf of his Defence team, I'm going to ask you some questions. In response to my colleague Bulatovic's question, you explained where and when and which posts you held during your career. I'm going to ask you a question relating to that. You said that then Colonel Mrksic was your commander. For how long was your commander?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: If you mean my immediate commander, one year, maybe a couple months more than a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Given that is a substantial period, and you're referring to the period where he was your immediate commander, I would like to start with what Mr. Bulatovic asked you with regard to Mr. Sljivancanin towards the end of his examination, and I'm going to ask you towards the beginning. As far as you knew Colonel Mrksic as a commander, what can you say about Mr. Mrksic, both as a commander and as a person?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: As in the case of the question of Mr. Bulatovic with regard to Mr. Sljivancanin, I must express a reservation as to my competence to assess my superior officer. My opinion, however, is that Colonel Mrksic was a professional, very correct, was an expert and -- in one word: A good officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Paunovic. My colleague Bulatovic also asked you this: When and how many times you testified before your testimony here in this court, and you cited three such instances. First, in 1999, before the military court in Belgrade; is that right? That was your first testimony. And then two times subsequent to that. Do you recall your statements given then? Have you refreshed your memory by perusing those statements soon before coming to this court?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: It can be said that I have refreshed my memory. Of course, I still cannot recall now what I said in each of these statements. By this, I mean the hours and time in certain statements, what was contentious was the date. But during proofing with a lawyer, he pointed out some of the quotes from my previous statements, and that would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, if we were to neglect some of your doubts as to dates, but can you say or can it be said, since you testified before the court and you had to take a solemn declaration then, can it be said that you told the truth as to the facts? Of course, dates may be incorrect.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Not only can it be said, but I did tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to ask the usher to hand a statement of -- a copy of your statement to the Prosecution and the military court in Belgrade to consult in the event I ask you something about those statements, but do not consult them before I do so. Mr. Paunovic, I'm going to ask you something that was the subject of your interview with representatives of the OTP, but I'm going to ask you directly, to see whether you remember that. Do you remember that a document had been put to you, an order of the 1st Military District, dated the 18th of November, signed by General Zivota Panic; and that this document was shown to you and that you expressed your views with regard to that document? If necessary, we're going to put the order on the screen so that you can see it. Perhaps that will jog your memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Exhibit 415. Could it please be shown on the screen. Can the witness see the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You can have a look, can't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then can we have it lifted a bit so that we see the further text of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to paragraphs 5, 8, and 3, in particular, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you've had a look, could we see paragraph 8 now as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You've read it, right? Thank you. Do you perhaps remember that in relation to this order or, generally speaking, you were giving answers to the Prosecutor, and do you remember what you said in relation to this in your answer or do you need to have your memory jogged through the statement itself? But if you remember, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Domazet, I am aware of this order. I first saw it, as you said yourself, before the investigators of The Hague Tribunal in Belgrade. So I cannot quote myself in the statement, which I believe is only natural. And in the statement, roughly, I said the following: That I was not aware of this particular order but that the commander did make us aware of the following: I think that I stated there that similar orders in relation to the Geneva Convention were, on several occasions, addressed by the brigade command, and he gave us orders in order to act properly towards prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. You talked about that, the implementation of the Geneva Convention, and that your commander told you about that. And you also stated your views about what is here, that is to say, revenge, retaliation by local persons. Can you remember what you said about that, if you don't look at the document? Do you know about such cases of revenge?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I personally was not aware of any cases of retaliation. Since you're talking about this order now, in the beginning of the order, you can see that it was not sent only to the command of the Guards Brigade but to all subordinate levels. So one cannot deduce on the basis of this that it was happening in our area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I agree with you. It is certainly possible that it pertained to other zones too. That's why I asked you whether you were aware of any such cases of local revenge in your zone.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No. I repeat once again: I did not hear of any such thing and I did not see any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you please look at your statement now, paragraph 51. In the English version, it is also 51.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note that they have not received any documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I'm going to read it out and you're going to tell me whether I read it out properly and whether that is your statement and whether you have any comments with regard to that as to whether it's correct or not. It says that a document was shown to you here. I'm not going to read out all of it. 1614-81/81, issued by the 1st Military District, on the 18th of November, 1991. 81/82, there's a mistake in the transcript. Sorry, it is actually 82/81. That is what it says in your statement: "As for paragraph 5, (prevention of disobedience, appearances that are not fitting for the military), and paragraph 8, (that units of the TO committed acts of revenge and retaliation), I recall that similar orders were regularly issued by Operations Group South. I'm not aware of any such cases of revenge on the part of members or units of the local Serb TO. As I mentioned previously, in the zone of responsibility of the 2nd Assault Platoon, there weren't any TO units. I did not see any act of revenge and I have not been informed that any such things took place." Have I read your statement correctly? Is that your statement? Have you got anything to say perhaps by way of comment?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I could make a comment. I signed the statement in English. There's probably a mistake in the translation. It is not assault platoon, it is assault detachment. It's towards the end of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. I read it the way it's written here, but you are correcting it now, that it could only be the 2nd Assault Detachment. You have no other objections, if I understand you correctly. Do you remember during that interview whether you talked about the implementation of the Geneva Convention on any other occasion? And did you make any comments about whether you and your soldiers were sufficiently aware of the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Now, whether I testified along similar lines, well, possibly before the special court; I cannot be sure of that. But all JNA officers, including myself, were aware of the provisions of the Geneva Convention from 1949. I am primarily referring to how armed forces act in the situations that we were talking about, that is to say, vis-a-vis the population, prisoners, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. So with regard to this subject, I have no further questions. The next topic that I would like to deal with is what you testified about earlier on, and some of it you referred to today as well, and that is with regard to your briefings at the command in Negoslavci. Do you remember that you spoke about that in your previous statements, not only today?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yesterday I think that you spoke more about a specific day, a particular briefing on the 19th, whereas my question refers to briefings in general. How often did you personally attend these briefings? I'm actually only referring to the briefings that took place in the evening, between 1700 and 1800 hours, at the command in Negoslavci, in view of the obligations that you had in the assault detachment and the other obligations you had?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I always attended briefings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can I understand your answer to mean that you were there practically every evening or quite literally every day?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The briefings usually took place - I mean the regular briefings - usually took place around 1800 hours, as I've already said. Perhaps - well, I don't remember now - there were a few times when they were held in the morning, but that primarily had to do with being handed out certain tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, that's why I asked you about these regular briefings, as we've been calling them here, that took place in the afternoon, or rather, it is already the evening, isn't it? You said that you attended practically every one of them.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about the other officers? Did they come to these briefings regularly, too, or were there some exceptions? What did you see, yourself?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: As for the other officers, the subordinate commanders, as far as I can remember, were present at all briefings. As for members of the command, I could not remember now whether they attended all the briefings, because sometimes certain members of the brigade command, at the time of the briefings, had some tasks. And I cannot remember any of them specifically right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Oh, yes, well, you made a distinction there between the subordinate commanders and the members of the command. Could you explain to the Trial Chamber, to the rest of us, who these other members of the command were and who sometimes were not present all the time because of other tasks they may have had.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm just going to mention the inner circle of the command, so to speak. I'm referring to the Chief of Staff of the brigade, the chief of the security organ, perhaps somebody from the operations and training department or organ. Those are the ones I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. So, to be quite certain, those are the ones you meant when you said that they were absent sometimes, as opposed to yourself and the other subordinates who were there practically every time. Did I understand your answer correctly?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you understood it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember whether there were any representatives of the local Territorial Defence at these briefings?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: These local TOs, as you've called them, were not present at briefings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I'm asking you that because you gave a similar answer, or rather, an identical answer, when you were interviewed by the investigators of the OTP. So now I would like to ask straight away about that, too, and you spoke about that as well in one of your statements; whether at that time you knew Dusan Jaksic.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And did you know Stanko Vujanovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot give a specific answer to your question; namely, that I knew him. I know who this person is because, on one occasion, in Vukovar, I encountered him. But I do not know, and I did not know then, what his position was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When I'm asking you this, I'm actually referring to that period, of course, October/November, up until those days, up until the end, not later. One more thing. At that time, did you know Miroljub Vujevic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know him either.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: We may go back to the issue of the briefings that you discussed today, but I would like to take this order. First, what transpired that afternoon that you referred to, and that is your role in securing the hospital. You said that you had a task to hold positions between the water-tower and Mitnica, when you received orders relayed by the Chief of Staff to go in the direction of the hospital; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: First, the action that you were engaged in, did this mean that this action was finished or was just a part of your subordinate sent towards the hospital and the others stayed behind? Could you please explain this situation further for us?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: The task that I explained included -- involved the engagement of two companies. That task was not achieved and fulfilled in its entirety. One company, the 1st Company, continued on that task, and having received the order to secure the hospital, as I said, I ordered the commander of the 4th Company to set out towards the hospital to fulfil this task.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember, in the preceding action between the water-tower and Mitnica, you explained the goal, to detect remaining elements or members of paramilitary forces or detect unexploded mines. Did you encounter anybody? Did you capture any members of the paramilitary Croatian units, you or your troops?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No. There were no captured members of the Croatian paramilitary forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you reached the hospital, you explained your orders, what was done; the search, the securing of the hospital. I'm not going to dwell on that, but I'm going to ask you about something that you said in response to a question by my learned colleague, which refers to the taking away of Marin Vidic, Bili. First of all, who ordered you to take Marin Vidic, Bili, to Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot really specify whether somebody phoned me -- not phoned me, but through radio contact. But I was told what I was supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Before you transported that person, had you ever seen that person; and if so, where?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: That person was in the hospital, which means that I saw him immediately before taking him away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When was that, on the first evening or the first day that you reached the hospital, or some other time?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for having to rise to my feet. In response to my question, the witness said that it was on the 19th that he took Vidic Bili to Negoslavci immediately before going to the briefing to the command. I believe that such hypothetical questions should not be allowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think I would interfere with Mr. Domazet's question, Mr. Bulatovic. Carry on, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You heard my question concerning said Vidic. You said that you saw him immediately before. My question would be: When did you take him to Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: On the 19th. I can't recall the hour. I cannot really recall, but I can give you a range, a period: Between 2100 hours and 2200 hours. This takes place after the briefing had ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: As far as I can understand your words, you came back from the briefing and then you received an order - you do not recall from whom, through the radio - to take this person to Negoslavci. Was this the only instance that you saw him or took them there -- you saw him either at Negoslavci, at Vukovar, or in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: This is the only time that I took him there. As I said, I handed him over at the place I specified, and after that I never saw him in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you do not know whether he was returned the following night, subsequent days. Did I understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid you haven't grasped my answer fully. I said that I never saw him, but I'm sure that he did not return to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: This is exactly why I'm asking you this question. There were statements to the effect that that person returned to hospital, but if you don't know anything about that, I'm not going to press this matter further.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: These may be statements provided by other people. My statement is that, with responsibility, I state that he did not return to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would it surprise you that that person gave such a statement and that he was taken to Negoslavci around 7.30, 8.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: That person may say whatever that person pleases. As to the time, whether his 7.30 is correct to the same extent that my claim of after 8.00 p.m. is also correct. But I have to reiterate that I'm not stating decidedly that this took place at 2000 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Please take a look, Mr. Paunovic, to the -- at the statement before you given to the military court in Belgrade around these facts. I believe it's towards the middle of the page, paragraph 2, maybe 17th row, in the second paragraph. I'm going to read it out to you and you will tell me whether it really states so.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, which page?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Page 3, 17th row. It starts with: "I remember that day ..."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not have the document; interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I'm going to read this sentence: "I recall this day that I, sometime around 900 hours, pursuant to an order of the brigade security organ, took Marin Vidic to the command post of the brigade. And Marin Vidic is a Croatian government's commissioner who was located at the hospital. I drove him and left him at the command post, and then I returned to the hospital. And in the meantime, Vesna Bosanac was taken there." You have managed to locate that part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: First, my question referring to the time indication, 9.00 in the morning; is that correct? And is your testimony as to the orders and the facts surrounding Vesna Bosanac, which was for the first time mentioned here, are these correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: As to the indicated time, it does say in this statement 9.00. It doesn't state whether it's in the a.m. or the p.m. But with full responsibility, I say, and I remember this very well, that it was dark. It was night-time when I took Marin Vidic. Secondly, I see that I gave this statement as to somebody from the security organ relaying to me the order, but now, nor then, I do not recall specifically who relayed that order to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: It doesn't say "relayed," it says "order." So would you agree with me that it follows from this that somebody ordered you, not relayed an order to you? Do you have any other explanation?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I just recently explained that the order was relayed to me through radio communication, but I cannot recall who exactly that person was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall anything about Vesna Bosanac? Has this jogged your memory with regard to her being taken there?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know, partially, something about that. She was taken there but after Marin Vidic. She was taken to Negoslavci, but I cannot recall who drove her there, who took her there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. At any rate, you did not. But you recall that she was taken there after Vidic, Bili, was taken there; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: As you stated today, responding to my colleague Bulatovic's questions, it follows that on the 19th, you attended the regular briefing, and that, in your opinion, it lasted around two hours. Have I understood today's testimony correctly?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you've understood me correctly. But I reiterate: With such time distance, whether we spent one, one and a half, two hours, me and the other commanders, at the command most, I really cannot remember. Maybe even longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. But you state today that you attended that briefing that evening.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Please take a look at the same testimony, slightly above the portion of the text that we examined just now. Second paragraph, maybe 12th row, it states, and I quote, and you are going to verify whether I quoted you correctly or not. "On that first night, only this company did security service, and I stayed at the hospital until approximately 0100 hours, after midnight, when I returned to my command post, which was located in the area of the Vuteks football ground, in the Radnicka Street." So if I read this correctly, there's no mention of your going to Negoslavci or that you were absent for one or two hours. Do you agree with this: You can read the whole of your statement and tell us whether it indicates that you were at Negoslavci, at the briefing, that evening.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: It would take me more time to read my entire statement, but probably the president of the military court, Colonel Gojevic, never asked me anything about that. I answered questions put to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I agree that it's possible that he did not ask you about that specifically; it's possible that he did not know about that. But do you agree with me that on the basis of this statement of yours it seems that all the way up to 0100 hours, you were at the hospital, near the hospital, and that it is only then that you went to your command post. You did not mention any departures to Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid that you didn't really quite understand this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: This statement is not long, by the way. If you wish, you can have a look at it and you can see whether you mention that particular departure at any point. But if not, let's not waste any time over that. Do you remember whether this was referred to when you spoke to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal, whether you talked about that? I'm talking about the meeting, the briefing, that you left the position near the hospital and that you came back.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Domazet, I did not leave my position. This is a question of terminology. Secondly, I said a few moments ago, from this distance now, I cannot recall everything I said in each and every statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: It's not referred to anywhere that you attended the briefing. If you wish, you can have a look at this later and then perhaps something can be said about this. That's why I'm asking you once again: Are you sure that you attended the briefing that night too?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that on the 19th of November I attended the briefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said that you were there and that future tasks were discussed, but I did not quite understand what you said, whether the evacuation of the hospital or this triage was part of your tasks, the triage of persons who were brought in there. I mean, was that referred to at all?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: What was referred to that evening was the evacuation of the hospital. As for a detailed elaboration of this operation, there wasn't any while I was at the command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, that's my question precisely, whether it is possible that this was talked about after the meeting that you attended, as you keep saying, and whether that was perhaps at some other meeting with higher officers, because you said that this meeting was attended by members of the command and all subordinate officers.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I allow for the possibility that perhaps the brigade commander elaborated some order, but I personally do not know about any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. On the following day, because you possibly do not know what happened on that day afterwards, did anyone tell you about any specific assignments or tasks; and if so, did anyone tell you about that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I did not see any such order, and no one conveyed that kind of order to me. I'm not aware of any such order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Well, my question now is: How did you act on the following day, when the evacuation of the hospital started, if you personally did not receive any order from anyone, or any task?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I have already responded to these questions, in part, during the first part of my testimony. During the evacuation, I saw officers from outside the brigade. Specifically, I saw Colonel Pavkovic. Maybe at that point I thought that he was in charge of that activity, but to this day I'm not sure. But I knew what my tasks were, even without these orders, and, as I've already said, that is to frisk these persons who were getting out of the hospital and to secure the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You mentioned Colonel Pavkovic. He did not belong to your brigade, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, he did not belong to our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know in what capacity he was in Vukovar then?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in what capacity he was there, I cannot respond to that. But I knew him from before that, that he worked in the cabinet of the Federal Secretary for National Defence; that was his workplace. Otherwise, I often saw him in Negoslavci, primarily at briefings. That is to say, that I could not really say anything about his role.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: At this meeting, at this briefing, that you talked about, was any reference made to the 1st Military District and any order issued by the 1st Military District about the evacuation of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And do you remember whether the hospital in Vukovar was in the area of responsibility of your brigade and generally of Operations Group South?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: It was not in our area of responsibility, if we're talking about these dates that we have been referring to until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Who could have possibly changed that decision about the area of responsibility of the hospital, that is in your view?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't understand what you were saying. Could you please clarify your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If, as you say, the hospital was not in the area of responsibility of your brigade or of Operations Group South up until those days, and if a change took place, who could have made this change of decision for the hospital to become part of the area of responsibility of Operations Group South?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, unless I'm mistaken, up until these dates that we have been referring to, the hospital belonged to the area of responsibility of Operations Group North. Again, I'm saying, unless I'm mistaken, the boundary between Operations Group South and Operations Group North was the Vuka River. Then, the logical conclusion would be that an order about a change of area of responsibility can, in this case, be issued by the commander of the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is this conclusion of yours based on the fact that this was the superior command of both Operations Group South and Tactical Group North?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But if I understand you correctly, you don't know anything more about this, whether the command of the 1st Military District issued any kind of orders related to the evacuation of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I have no such knowledge. I am not saying that they did not issue any orders, but I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, as for the explanations you gave regarding your work on the 20th of November, in the morning, in front of the hospital, you were talking about the way in which your soldiers searched or frisked persons there. My question is: Did this pertain to all the persons who were leaving the hospital; namely, women, children, men? Or were there different groups there that were getting out of the hospital and that were not submitted to these checks and searches that you have been talking about?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: All persons, if I understand you correctly, all persons who were leaving the hospital were searched. Now, it depends on when and in what time-period this was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I am interested in whether this pertained to women, men, children, irrespective of gender or age, whether all persons were searched.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: All persons were searched.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Where did women go, if they went separately, and where did men go?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. And that was not my task to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to rephrase this question. Were special groups set up after persons left the hospital, that is to say, special groups of civilians and special groups of those who were considered suspects after the triage; namely, that they were suspected of having taken part in something which then required further checks?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: As you said yourself, there is this one group of suspects, so to speak. As for others, other groups, it was mixed, irrespective of gender and age, where they were going to. During the introductory part, I talked about that, I talked about where they went, but I could not know about that for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I don't want to go back to your statements and remind you of all of this, but I don't think this really matters that much. I think you talked about a group that was returned from the Croatian border, that you had received information to that effect. You are saying that there were both men and women there, if I understood you correctly. Are those the ones who were searched by you but who were in some other group, as opposed to these who were taken to the buses that have been referred to?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC
utterances.text: In one of my statements I spoke about that group. I did not mean that it only had to do with the people from the hospital, because there were people from other parts of town there as well. Some expressed a wish to go to Croatia; others, to Serbia. As far as I can remember, this has to do with the border - I don't know which part exactly - between Serbia and Croatia. Croatia did not want to receive these civilians who wanted to go to Croatia. Now, who was that problem resolved later? I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Those who were going to the buses are going to be our next topic, but I'm afraid we're not going to be able to finish tonight.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that I will deal with this subject tomorrow morning, then, and finish it tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Domazet. We will resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 7th day of November, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
